scope: Primary literature model-scope and validation comparison. Facts and our inferences are separated. No solver runs or production edits.

sources.citation: O. Boine-Frankenheim and V. Kornilov, Implementation and Validation of Space Charge and Impedance Kicks in the Code PATRIC for Studies of Transverse Coherent Instabilities in the FAIR Rings, ICAP2006 WEA3MP04, pp267–270.
sources.location: p267 Eqs2–3 and assumptions paragraph; p269 validation examples
verified_primary_facts: Transverse fields come from 2D Poisson solves at longitudinal grid positions.
Assumes bunch length much greater than transverse beam and pipe dimensions.
Assigns the bunch-centre lattice position to all slices, neglecting fast transverse-envelope changes across the bunch.
Validation includes coasting-beam noise spectra and analytic stability boundaries, not a finite hard-ended curved-tube field comparison.
sources.contrast_inference: Our large global aspect ratio supports a slice approximation in the bulk, but passing these stability observables cannot certify one-percent weak curvature or end-field accuracy.

sources.citation: H. Bartosik, Code description: pyORBIT, CERN ABP-CWG, 2 March2017.
verified_primary_facts: The model named 2.5D projects transverse charge onto a single grid and weights transverse kicks by local line density.
Optional longitudinal forces use a line-density derivative with a transverse-uniform-beam assumption.
A separately named slice-by-slice 2D model bins on a 3D grid and differentiates its sliced potential for transverse and longitudinal kicks.
Separate longitudinal models include on-axis round-pipe impedance and a special version with radial dependence.
sources.contrast_inference: 2.5D is a family label. OPALX combines independent slice solves and a fixed-g longitudinal closure; one cannot transfer the capabilities or validation of every similarly named model to it.
sources.access: Web reader403; primary PDF downloaded successfully and all17pages text-extracted locally.

sources.citation: ImpactX26.10 official documentation, Parameters: Python, space-charge model properties.
verified_primary_facts: Distinguishes 2D long-unbunched, 2p5D line-density-weighted transverse fields plus longitudinal density derivative, full3D, and Gaussian3D/2p5D models.
For Gauss2p5D, default longitudinal scale1.103 gamma sigma_z minimizes the on-axis longitudinal-field L2 error for a long3D Gaussian bunch.
For a long bunch in a perfectly conducting pipe, recommends the pipe radius as the scale instead.
FFT field solver uses integrated Green functions with open boundaries.
sources.contrast_inference: A longitudinal normalization selected for Gaussian free space is profile-dependent. It does not establish the hard-end field of our uniform elliptical source or validate curvature.

sources.citation: ImpactX26.08 official example, Momentum Kick in the2.5D Gaussian Space Charge Model.
sources.location: Setup and analytic prediction; embedded test code lines288–333,626–670
verified_primary_facts: Uses an initially cold round-Gaussian100MeV electron bunch in a1m drift with one space-charge kick.
Example rms transverse sizes40micrometres and rms ct1mm; charge1nC.
Checks particle momentum changes against Qiang2025 Eqs31–32 for the same reduced model.
Embedded PIC acceptance tolerances are2% rms/6.3% maximum transverse and20% rms/40% maximum longitudinal, normalized by predicted component maxima. These are test tolerances, not measured errors.
sources.contrast_inference: Our frozen-field comparison follows the useful single-kick/field-first validation pattern, but additionally tests the reduced model against independent3D Coulomb fields. This example supplies no universal1% claim.

sources.citation: Y.-S. Yuan, O. Boine-Frankenheim and I. Hofmann, Intensity limitations due to space charge for bunch compression in synchrotrons, PRAB21,074201(2018).
sources.location: SecIIA Eq1; SecIIC pp3–4; TableI p4; Fig5
verified_primary_facts: Uses1D longitudinal plus2D transverse space charge because compressed bunches remain long compared with transverse sizes.
Starts with parabolic longitudinal and3sigma-truncated Gaussian transverse distributions.
SIS18 example uses uranium73+,295MeV/u,216m circumference and half-length78m compressed to6m.
Compares coupled-envelope and PIC observables, including rms sizes and resonance/emittance-growth behaviour.
Longitudinal geometry factor is0.5+2ln(pipe radius/beam radius).
sources.contrast_inference: This establishes usefulness for smooth-profile synchrotron dynamics under its closure, not our open-space sharp-end point fields. Our beta0.001 and electrostatic frozen source differ substantially.

sources.citation: O. Boine-Frankenheim, I. Hofmann, J. Struckmeier and S. Appel, Artificial collisions, entropy and emittance growth in computer simulations of intense beams, NIMA770,164–168(2015).
verified_primary_facts: Finite macro-particle sampling adds numerical noise and diffusion to self-consistent PIC dynamics.
Noise-driven growth depends on macro-particle count and tune shift.
Studies2D/2.5D synchrotron models and explains the need to balance particle population, grid resolution and interpolation.
sources.contrast_inference: Our initially nonconvergent polar-source fields cannot be interpreted as model error merely by refining the mesh. The quiet-source, sampling and matched-mesh controls are necessary; frozen checks alone also do not certify long-term emittance accuracy.
sources.access: Primary publisher abstract/introduction/section previews read; full article not obtained.

sources.citation: O. Boine-Frankenheim, I. Hofmann and J. Struckmeier, Artificial Collisions, Entropy and Emittance Growth in Computer Simulations of Intense Beams, IPAC2014 TUPRI017.
verified_primary_facts: Derives diffusion/entropy relations and studies numerical-friction scaling against simulations.
Warns that PIC noise can contaminate long-term beam-loss predictions; increasing particle count and using higher-order interpolation or density smoothing controls it.
sources.contrast_inference: Supports separately checking numerical source sampling and eventual long-term tracking, rather than treating a converged frozen field as full dynamical validation.

sources.citation: M. J. L. de Hoon, E. P. Lee, J. J. Barnard and A. Friedman, Cold phase fluid model of the longitudinal dynamics of space-charge-dominated beams, Phys.Plasmas10,855–861(2003); original LBNL manuscript dated1March2002.
sources.location: Original manuscript SecI; SecII Eqs4–16; SecIII
sources.access: Root read the complete original author-uploaded LBNL manuscript through the web full-text extraction. Journal citation metadata independently confirmed; full journal text was not read. Institutional endpoint returned403.
verified_primary_facts: Local g approximation requires uniform density and slowly varying beam semiaxes/line density on the pipe-radius scale.
Identifies breakdown near ends, for short compressed beams and at shocks.
Derives a nonlocal Fourier–Bessel field; recovers local g by Taylor expansion.
Finite-radius compressed-slice field remains bounded; WARP(r,z) solver replaces g for end dynamics.
sources.contrast_inference: Supports a known hard-end approximation limitation, not a universal2.5D failure or numerical boundary bug.
sources.limits: Kernel is transverse-averaged Ez for a straight circularized beam in an infinite circular conducting pipe. ItsR is pipe radius, not bend radius. It does not quantitatively predict our open elliptical curved-tube point fields.

conclusions_ours: The2.5D label alone does not specify how longitudinal fields, transverse variation or geometry are handled.
Global slenderness does not establish slow longitudinal variation at a sharp end.
A1% normalization to the13.07V/m transverse characteristic field permits errors larger than the entire0.055V/m curvature signal; the midpoint response needs its own error measure.
Frozen Coulomb tests establish a field-operator benchmark; matching rms sizes, tune shifts or a reduced-model analytic kick establishes different observables.
